title: Director, Battery Asset Management
location: Charlottesville, VA; Moorestown, NJ; New York, NY; Richmond, VA; Tysons, VA
description: About Us Madison Energy Infrastructure is hiring a Director of Battery Asset Management to build and run the operating platform behind our national, distributed, battery fleet. We have 80 MW of batteries operating today across 30 sites and 5 states, expect that fleet to triple next year and double the following year, with $2 billion of battery deployment ahead of us. The goal is simple: get the operating system right now, while the fleet is still manageable, so that it works when at scale. About You You've spent years elbow-deep in battery systems — you can read a three-line diagram without help, and you know an OEM's manual well enough to push back on their own engineers. You've managed contracts and you've managed people, and you're just as comfortable owning a preventative maintenance program as you are picking up the phone when a site goes down. You'd rather build something from scratch than inherit someone else's system, and you want to own the numbers that come with that. Key Responsibilities In year one, expect to be a player-coach: you'll manage the Battery Asset Manager, but you'll also be hands-on yourself — on the phone with OEMs, troubleshooting failures remotely, reviewing alarms, negotiating O&M agreements, visiting sites, escalating warranty claims, and making sure batteries dispatch when they're supposed to. That hands-on work is also how you'll build the operating system this role exists to create — you will own: Fleet Performance  - Own fleet performance against target (97%+ monthly availability, <1% missed dispatch, 100% preventative maintenance compliance, ≤7-day MTTR on corrective issues, zero warranty violations, no OEM escalation delay beyond 72 hours). Report against these numbers and drive resolution when a site is down. title: Senior Director, Digital Infrastructure Partnerships
description: The Role Following Madison’s groundbreaking Community Infrastructure announcement to develop 1 GW an d mobilize up to $2 billion in capital , we are seeking to make a critical hire to lead and own partnerships with digital infrastructure customers and partners (Aggregators, Hyperscalers, Edge Data Centers, and other large power users in the digital space). This pivotal person will report directly to the Chief Development Officer and be responsible for securing the crucial partnerships and investment-grade offtake — at an acceptable price and term, for a specified volume — that will allow MEI to meet its ambitious  Community Infrastructure goals. Working closely with Development, Origination, Commercial Analysis, Regulatory/Policy, Legal, and the MEI Executive Team, the Senior Director will own the evolution of partnerships and customer relationships from the first conversation, into memorandum of understanding and exclusivity, and into binding commercial agreements. This is a partnership-oriented role built on durable, high-trust relationships where s uccess is measured through executed term sheets and binding agreements  that convert into megawatts under contract .   As part of our Community Infrastructure announcement, we defined a new goal to Build Here. Benefit Here whereby we are attempting to partner with local communities, utilities, government agencies, etc. to listen to their concerns with power/data center development and develop our projects in ways that benefit local communities. This person will be critical in coordinating that story with the community benefits teams at Digital Infrastructure Companies and at times also acting as the face of our efforts in those local communities.
